correctness.rationale: The exact conditional-on-absence identity Cov(I_i,G)=Pr(I_i=0)(G_pop-G_excluding_i) reduces algebraically to the stated finite falling-factorial sum. The symmetric identity N sum a_i w_i(t-a_i)=sum_{i<j}a_i a_j(a_i-a_j)(w_j-w_i) and weight antitonicity prove both nonnegative terms and the sharp lower bound. Degenerate profiles and complete-detection cutoffs give a necessary-and-sufficient zero classification. Exact independent subset and composition enumerations plus the closed formula agree for all 2,375 cases of N<=12. No experiment substitutes for the full proof.

value.rationale: The joint behavior of species richness and sample pairwise diversity determines uncertainty and interpretation when ecological inventories use both indices. Their finite-sample positive dependence is not automatic from their separate means or variances; the proof yields an attained, abundance-sensitive quantitative lower bound and precise saturation zeros, in contrast to the known iid theorem that remains strictly positive for nondegenerate parent laws. These are structural exact finite-rarefaction statements, not arbitrary numerical slices.
